claims.text: Removing Mn from equiatomic Cr–Mn–Fe–Co–Ni reduces magnetic frustration.
Reduced magnetic frustration lowers the barrier for a dislocation-induced FCC-to-HCP transformation.
The dislocation-induced FCC-to-HCP transformation is accompanied by nanotwin formation.
The proposed transformation mechanism is activated in Mn-free quaternary or ternary derivatives such as CrCoNi.
Activation of the proposed transformation increases work hardening and improves the strength–ductility balance relative to the quinary alloy.
Equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi has a single-phase FCC structure.
Equiatomic CrCoNi has a single-phase FCC structure.
Mn-free quaternary derivatives such as equiatomic CrFeCoNi can be obtained as single-phase FCC materials through the same thermomechanical route used for the quinary alloy.
Mn removal is the controlled compositional intervention used to compare the quinary alloy with its Mn-free subsets.
The comparison should use identical room-temperature uniaxial tensile conditions, equivalent grain sizes, and initially single-phase FCC microstructures.
A dislocation-triggered FCC-to-HCP transformation and associated nanotwinning mediate work hardening.
Mn exhibits magnetically frustrated behavior in the CrMnFeCoNi alloy because its preferred antiparallel spin alignment cannot be fully satisfied among the other magnetic constituents.
Removing Mn permits more coherent alignment of Ni and Co magnetic moments.
Nanoscale twins or HCP plates interact with dislocations, delay failure, and enhance ductility.
Magnetic frustration from Mn suppresses the deformation-induced phase transformation in the quinary alloy and thereby lowers its work-hardening response.
At room temperature, Mn-free quaternary or ternary alloys will have greater work hardening and increased yield strength and/or ductility relative to CrMnFeCoNi.
CrCoNi has been reported to possess higher cryogenic strength, ductility, and fracture toughness than its quinary parent and other equiatomic FCC derivatives.
The magnitude of any strength or ductility change may depend on processing parameters and measurement sensitivity.

The hypothesis is falsified if the Mn-free alloy shows neither a significant mechanical-property improvement nor a difference in FCC-to-HCP transformation or nanotwinning relative to the quinary control.
